notes.title: Nintendo Switch version submitted! Let’s celebrate with a Steam update! 🤖💨
notes.notes:
Big news, [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] fans!

The Nintendo Switch edition of [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] has been submitted to Nintendo for certification.

Once it’s passed certification we’ll put it up on the Nintendo eShop, and we’ll be launching the official final version on Steam the same day. In other words, after a long time in early access, [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] is very, very close to a full official release on Steam!

[img]https://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/BigRobotTyping.gif[/img]

This is a huge milestone for us. Our Early Access players have been incredibly patient with us tweaking the gameplay, experimenting with new features, and just generally changing stuff around. We’ve learned a lot from your feedback and all of you have helped us to make [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] the best game it could possibly be. We’re absolutely thrilled to be so close to delivering a complete game to you all.

To celebrate this milestone, we have uploaded a new Steam build for you all. This isn’t the official final version quite yet, but it does have a pile of new content, bug fixes, and polish that we’re sure you’ll love.

Thanks as always for your support. It feels like we’re finally coming to the end of a very long journey (we started making [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] almost 4 years ago!) and it’s been wonderful to have so many of you awesome people join us along the way.

To keep on top of the latest news, check out our [url=https://twitter.com/cc_content]Twitter account[/url].

See you on the other side of the official release!

Much robotic love,
Scott and Ed of Considerable Content

notes.title: New features coming as we close in on our official v1.0 release
notes.notes:
Hello you awesome speed-runners!

We’ve been a little quiet for the last couple of months because we’ve been hard at work on the PC and Nintendo Switch versions of the game with an expanded team. We don’t have a concrete release date to announce quite yet, but we can tell you that Nintendo Switch and Steam versions will launch on the same day, and we’re really close to announcing the date.

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/SoClose1.gif[/img]
We’re SO CLOSE!

In the meantime, we have some cool stuff to announce. In addition to new PC features, while working on porting the game to Switch we designed a bunch of new features that we liked so much we decided backwards-port them into the PC as well. (“Backwards-port” is totally a real thing and definitely not a term we just made up.)

Some of the cool things that will be in the game when it launches include:[list]
[*]Major improvements to the user interface (seriously, it’s SO much better)
[*]Gameplay video recording and one-touch screenshots to capture your finest moments
[*]A full set of Steam achievements and trading cards for the completionists
[*]A major overhaul of balancing and difficulty to make the whole experience flow better
[/list]

Of course, we have to take [i]some[/i] time off, and over the holiday period we got to play some games that other people have made (instead of just testing the Black Hole over and over). Scott got stuck into [i]Uncharted: Lost Legacy[/i], the re-released [i]Deadpool[/i] game, [i]Rise of the Tomb Raider[/i], and [i]Dream Daddy[/i]. Meanwhile, Ed got deeply into [i]Secret World Legends[/i], [i]Overwatch[/i], [i]Luigi's Mansion 2[/i], and [i]Offworld Trading Company[/i].

Thanks for being an early adopter. All of your feedback, suggestions, and bug reports have been vital for making [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] the game it is, and we’re eternally grateful.

That’s all for now, but stay tuned! We’ll have more to announce…

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/SoClose2.png[/img]

 - Ed, Scott, and the Considerable Content crew

notes.title: Development update! Phew, we’ve been doing a lot of stuff...
notes.notes:
Hello everybody!

We’ve been working our shiny robot butts off getting [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] finished, which is really exciting. We started compiling a list so we could write this update and we were a little shocked about just how much we’ve been getting done! Here’s a quick summary...

[b]Building better boss battles![/b] We only have two boss battles so we want to make them perfect. We’ve put heaps of work into balancing fun and challenge, making them just the right level of difficulty.

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/Boss1.gif[/img]

[b]Delivering closure![/b] We’ve been putting together a really enjoyable “grand finale” that should be a satisfying payoff for players who manage to get all the way to the end.

[b]Tightening up the talk![/b] The story of the little robot and the galactic warlord has grown in the telling, so we’ve done a lot of rewriting on the dialogue and doing fresh recordings with our awesome voice talent.

[b]Shhh! Secret stuff![/b] Did you know that [i]Rogue Singularity[/i] has secret levels? No? Well, that’s because they’re secret! We’ve spent a lot of time recently on making these hidden levels as cool as possible.

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/BeeBrawl1.gif[/img]

[b]Prettying the place up![/b] Graphical upgrades have been coming along for lots of different elements of the game, especially robot special abilities and the black hole mode.

[b]Boring behind the scenes stuff![/b] A lot of our recent work has been super-important but not all that glamorous: fixing bugs, improving load times, tweaking the procedural generation systems, improving controller support, adding Steam achievements, and so much more.

Thanks so much for your support as we finish this final sprint toward the full release. We couldn’t have achieved this without our wonderful Early Access players. You rock!

 - Ed and Scott

notes.title: Content Update 1 - v0.60.1706
notes.notes:
We've been hard at work on Rogue Singularity and we've just pushed our first Early Access content update live to Steam. Please check out the notes below for what’s in this update.

[h1]Major Additions[/h1]
[list]
[*]New Daily Challenge mode

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/DailyChallenge1.gif[/img]

Once per day you'll be able to attempt to pass a shared global set of levels. Everyone playing the daily challenge that day will play the same levels and compete on a new daily leaderboard. Only one chance a day to be the best in the world, can you do it?

[*]New Brawl mode

[img]http://static01.considerablecontent.com/rogue/steam/RobotBrawl1.gif[/img]

Every week we'll release a new Brawl, which is a placeholder name for a mode where we get a bit experimental and sometimes a bit silly. We'll create a number of levels,  usually less than the other modes, that have some aspects of the normal game mixed up and experimented with. Things like level shape, level contents, or character abilities are up for grabs. For example, our first Brawl is all about the robotic enemies. We've absolutely filled the levels with them. Can you make it past them all?
[/list]
[h1]Other Improvements/Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Updated engine version. This update brings many bug fixes and better performance for certain PC spec configurations
[*]Improve controller hardware support by adding support for the new PS4 controller and fixing minor issues with other controllers
[*]Pressing the Esc key or the B button on Xbox controllers (or the equivalent on other controllers) while in a menu will now close the menu
[*]Enemies that throw projectiles at the player are now less likely to do so when you can’t see them
[*]Fix missing colliders on some props in Zone 5
[*]Fix some ambient sounds not looping correctly
[*]Improve music looping and crossfading
[/list]

Please give us your feedback, especially in regards to the two new game modes. We hope to make them major parts of the game and need your help to refine them.
